newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY 1997 MACRO GROWTH GOOD FOR RETAILERS - K&H.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY 1997 MACRO GROWTH GOOD FOR RETAILERS - K&H.

text.p: Macroeconomic improvement in Hungary in 1997 is expected to have a beneficial impact on retailers, Hungary's K&H Securities said in its monthly report on the Hungarian share market.
"We believe that slightly increasing disposable income and consumer spending are going to boost retailers' performance in coming years," analysts Robert Rethy and Szabolcs Varga said.

The analysts of K&H -- member of the Kereskedelmi Bank's financial group - put their votes on Csopak , which is increasingly involved in retail, but has interest in milling and cosmetics industries too.
"One of our favourite is Csopak, a retailer positioned in the more developed western region of the country," they said.
"According to our expectations the share price may reach 2,000 forints in 1997/98, therefore Csopak qualifies for a clear 'long-term buy'," the analysts said.
They said that with its new strategic partner, East European Food Fund, Csopak tries to match changing consumer habits by focusing on malls and on food retail in the future.

The fund acquired an over 30 percent stake in Csopak in mid-December by fully subscribing the whole of a 700-million forint private share issue which brought Csopak's issued share capital to 2.2 billion forints.
"We expect sales to rise at a pace higher than inflation... and earnings per share can be well above 400 forints despite the recent capital increase," the two analysts said.
Diversified retailer Fotex also seems to be well-positioned with strong presence in the newly built shopping malls in Budapest.
"In 1997 the company may experience a jump in sales and also some improvement in profitability, though the financial burden of the too generously priced convertible bonds is going to harm profits."
"We still regard investing in Fotex to be speculative but after the years of disappointment shareholders may now have higher hopes," Rethy and Varga said.
Packaging company Cofinec was "another promising investment," K&H Securities said, adding it maintained the 'buy' rating on Cofinec shares.

"Merger of the two Hungarian units is expected to result in cost savings and greater operational efficiency," they said, adding that better market positions for Cofinec Polska and Cofinec's Czech subsidiary would also improve outlook.
"We expect Cofinec to report a modest profit for 1997 after last year's losses," they said.
Cofinec has not yet released its 1996 results but reported losses for the first nine months.
